title: Collaboration with Git and GitHub
description: "Your team's repository: one place for the course material, your assignments and the trading game, with a teammate check before every hand-in."
---

***Git*** records every change to your project, so you can see who changed what and go back to any earlier state. ***GitHub*** hosts the repository online, so your team works on the same files without sending them around. Both are standard tools in finance and data science jobs.

![Bad file management can be a burden](figures/git-file-versions.png){fig-align="center" width="70%"}

We strongly encourage you to use Git and GitHub for your team work in this course. It is not required: you can hand in your assignments without it.

## Your team repository

Each team gets one private repository on GitHub for the whole semester, which we create for you: `advanced-empirical-finance/aef27-<team>`. It starts as a copy of the [course repository](https://github.com/advanced-empirical-finance/course-repository), with the R and Python environment, the `data` folder, the templates and the slides, and it stays connected to it, so new course material reaches you with one command. Only your team and the teaching team can see it.

1. Create a free [GitHub account](https://github.com/signup), if you do not have one. Your username does not have to be your real name. As a student, you can also apply for the [GitHub Student Developer Pack](https://education.github.com/pack), which includes GitHub Copilot.
2. Send us the GitHub usernames of everyone in your team.
3. Each of you receives an invitation by email. Accept it within seven days.

::: {.callout-warning title="TBD"}
The link to send your usernames follows.
:::

## Get the repository onto your computer

Each team member does this once.

1. In Positron, click *New*, then *New Folder from Git*, and paste the address of your team repository: `https://github.com/advanced-empirical-finance/aef27-<team>.git`. Sign in to GitHub when your browser asks.
2. Open the Terminal in that folder and connect the repository to the course repository, so you can pull new material later:

   ```bash
   git remote add upstream https://github.com/advanced-empirical-finance/course-repository.git
   git config pull.rebase false   # pulling merges, as described below
   ```

3. Install the environment, as in the [technical prerequisites](../exercises/technical-prerequisites.qmd): `uvr sync` and `uv sync`.
4. Put the licensed data from Absalon into the `data` folder, such as `crsp_monthly.parquet`. Git ignores them, so they never end up on GitHub.

## Where your work goes

Put everything your team writes into folders of its own: `assignment-1`, `assignment-2`, `assignment-3` and `trading-game`. To start an assignment, copy the template and `references.bib` from `mandatory-assignments` into the assignment's folder.

Do not edit the course's files (`lecture-slides`, `mandatory-assignments`, `data-raw`). Course updates change exactly these files; if you leave them alone, every update arrives without conflicts.

## The daily loop

Before you start, get your teammates' latest work. When you are done, or whenever you reach a step worth keeping, save it as a commit and share it:

```bash
git pull                           # your teammates' latest work
# ... work ...
git status                         # what has changed?
git add assignment-1
git commit -m "Estimate the tangency portfolio with monthly returns"
git push
```

The *Source Control* panel in Positron (`Ctrl+Shift+G`) does the same with buttons. A commit message says what you changed and why, in one line.

## Split the report so you do not get in each other's way

Git merges changes in different files, or in different parts of a file, by itself. It only stops when two of you change the same lines. So give each section of your report its own file and pull them into the report with includes:

```markdown
## Data

{{{< include sections/_data.qmd >}}}

## Results

{{{< include sections/_results.qmd >}}}
```

Each of you works in your own section file, and the report still renders from start to finish. Files whose names start with an underscore are not rendered on their own. If Git does report a conflict, it marks the lines in the file: keep the right version, delete the markers, then `git add` and `git commit`.

## Before you hand in: the teammate check as a pull request

The [quality criteria](assignment-quality-criteria.qmd) recommend that a teammate reproduces your report before you hand it in. A pull request is the natural place for this check.

1. **Whoever finishes the report** puts the final version on a branch of its own and pushes it:

   ```bash
   git switch -c assignment-1-check
   git push -u origin assignment-1-check
   ```

   On GitHub, click *Compare & pull request* and write what the teammate should check.

2. **A teammate** gets that version in a new folder, installs the environment from scratch, adds the licensed data and renders the report:

   ```bash
   git clone --branch assignment-1-check https://github.com/advanced-empirical-finance/aef27-<team>.git check-assignment-1
   cd check-assignment-1
   uvr sync
   uv sync
   # copy the licensed data into data/, then render assignment-1/report.qmd
   ```

   If it renders and the numbers match the PDF, approve the pull request on GitHub. If not, comment on what went wrong; fixes go into the same branch.

3. **Merge** the pull request on GitHub. Everyone then switches back with `git switch main` and runs `git pull`.

## New material from the course

When we announce new material, pull it from the course repository into your team repository, and push it so your teammates have it too:

```bash
git pull upstream main
git push
```

If you added packages of your own, Git may report a conflict in `uvr.toml`, `uvr.lock`, `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`. Keep the course's version, add your packages again and commit:

```bash
git checkout --theirs uvr.toml uvr.lock pyproject.toml uv.lock
uvr add <your R packages>
uv add <your Python packages>
git add uvr.toml uvr.lock pyproject.toml uv.lock
git commit -m "Course update; our packages added again"
```

## What never goes into Git

- **Licensed data**, such as CRSP. The `data` folder ignores everything except the public files of the course.
- **Your trading game token.** `set_token()` saves it in `.Renviron` (R) or `.env` (Python), which Git ignores. If a token ever ends up on GitHub, tell us and we replace it.
- **Large files**: GitHub refuses files over 100 MB. Save results as compact parquet files, or recompute them.

Run `git status` before every commit: it lists what would be added.

## Git with an AI assistant

Your AI assistant in Positron, or an agent such as Claude Code or GitHub Copilot, can run every command on this page and resolve most conflicts for you. Read what it changed before you commit (*Source Control* panel or `git diff`), and make sure the commit message says what the change does.

To learn more, read [Happy Git and GitHub for the useR](https://happygitwithr.com) by Jenny Bryan, which also applies to Python.
